intro: Feature preprocessing should learn its vocabulary from training data only. Holding that mapping fixed gives an honest picture of unseen categories during evaluation.
task: Fit a vocabulary on training categories only, then encode heldout unknowns distinctly.
requirements: Both inputs are sequences of strings, including empty strings. Assign training categories consecutive integer IDs from 0 in first-occurrence order. Return vocabulary, train_codes, heldout_codes, and unknown_positions for heldout; unseen heldout values encode as -1 and never extend the vocabulary.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Fit the mapping using training values before looking at heldout values.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Do not call setdefault while encoding heldout categories; that would leak new categories into the fitted mapping.

explanation: Feature preprocessing should learn its vocabulary from training data only. Holding that mapping fixed gives an honest picture of unseen categories during evaluation.
First-occurrence IDs make the fit deterministic for a fixed training order. Unknown heldout values use a reserved negative code and remain visible through their positions.
